"GAME TITLE: CALL OF ZOMBIES: ROUND WAR
1. GAME OVERVIEW
Create a high-end, photorealistic, first-person zombie survival shooter titled CALL OF ZOMBIES: ROUND WAR.
The game is a round-based zombie survival FPS inspired by classic arcade-style zombie survival games and modern military shooters.
Players must survive increasingly difficult waves of undead enemies while exploring detailed environments, collecting weapons, purchasing upgrades, unlocking restricted areas, discovering secrets, and fighting powerful boss zombies.
The experience should combine:
Intense first-person military gunplay.
Extremely realistic weapon models and animations.
Photorealistic character models.
Massive zombie hordes.
Cinematic lighting and environmental effects.
Detailed destruction and environmental storytelling.
Challenging round-based progression.
Cooperative multiplayer survival.
Hidden mysteries and Easter eggs.
The game should prioritize gameplay performance, atmosphere, immersion, and AAA visual quality.
2. GRAPHICS AND VISUAL QUALITY
Create the game using the highest graphical quality supported by the game engine.
Target an Unreal Engine 5-quality visual presentation.
Character graphics
Every playable character must feature:
Photorealistic facial geometry.
High-resolution skin textures.
Realistic eyes and facial expressions.
Detailed clothing materials.
Physically simulated clothing movement.
Realistic body proportions.
Detailed tactical equipment.
Realistic gloves, boots, helmets, and armor.
Facial animation during dialogue and cinematic scenes.
Zombie models must feature:
Extremely detailed decaying skin.
Exposed wounds and torn clothing.
Realistic blood and damage textures.
Different body types and proportions.
Unique facial structures.
Realistic movement and attack animations.
Visible damage that changes their appearance during combat.
Weapon graphics
Weapons must look and feel like authentic modern firearms.
Include:
High-resolution weapon textures.
Realistic metallic reflections.
Detailed weapon components.
Individual moving weapon parts.
Realistic muzzle flashes.
Weapon recoil animations.
Shell casing ejection.
Detailed reload animations.
Magazine removal and insertion.
Weapon inspection animations.
Realistic smoke and firing effects.
Dynamic flashlight illumination.
Visible weapon attachments.
Weapons should occupy the lower portion of the first-person screen, with realistic positioning and perspective.
Environment graphics
Every map should have:
High-resolution environmental textures.
Realistic terrain.
Detailed buildings and interiors.
Volumetric fog.
Dynamic shadows.
Realistic weather.
Destructible environmental objects.
Dynamic lighting.
Atmospheric particles.
Realistic water and reflections.
Flickering electrical equipment.
Environmental sound effects.
Use cinematic nighttime lighting, dramatic shadows, realistic fire, smoke, and atmospheric horror elements.
3. FIRST-PERSON GAMEPLAY
Create a fully immersive first-person perspective.
The player must have:
Smooth walking and sprinting.
Tactical sliding.
Crouching.
Jumping.
Mantling over obstacles.
Weapon aiming.
Hip-fire shooting.
Reloading.
Weapon swapping.
Melee attacks.
Grenade throwing.
Equipment deployment.
Implement realistic weapon sway, recoil, movement animations, and camera motion.
The player should feel like an actual soldier fighting for survival.
Include a customizable field of view, sensitivity settings, controller support, and adjustable graphics settings.
4. ROUND-BASED ZOMBIE SYSTEM
The main gameplay revolves around surviving endless zombie rounds.
Players begin on Round 1.
Each round introduces more zombies, stronger enemy variations, and increasingly aggressive behavior.
Round progression
Round 1–5:
Small zombie groups.
Slow-moving undead.
Basic weapons.
Limited ammunition.
Introduction to map exploration.
Round 6–10:
Larger zombie hordes.
Faster zombies.
Armored undead begin appearing.
Stronger enemy attacks.
Special enemies introduced.
Round 11–20:
Large enemy waves.
Explosive zombies.
Heavy armored zombies.
More aggressive AI.
Increased enemy health.
Round 21–30:
Extremely dangerous hordes.
Multiple special enemies.
Elite zombie variants.
Boss encounters.
Round 31+:
Endless survival difficulty.
Extremely large hordes.
Elite enemies appear more frequently.
Increased zombie speed and damage.
Randomized enemy combinations.
Every fifth round should feature a special event or challenging enemy encounter.
Every tenth round should feature a major boss battle.
Zombie AI behavior
Zombies must:
Detect players through sight and sound.
Follow player movement.
Surround players.
Break through barricades.
Attack doors and windows.
Climb through obstacles.
Chase players through buildings.
React to gunfire.
Change targets dynamically.
Coordinate attacks when surrounding players.
Zombies should never feel like stationary targets. Their movement should be unpredictable, aggressive, and frightening.
5. ZOMBIE ENEMY VARIATIONS
Create multiple unique enemy types.
Standard Walker
Slow-moving undead soldier or civilian. Weak individually but dangerous in groups.
Runner
Fast-moving zombie that sprints toward players and attempts to overwhelm them.
Armored Zombie
Former military personnel wearing damaged tactical armor. Requires additional ammunition to eliminate.
Brute
Massive mutated undead with enormous strength. Can break through barricades and knock players backward.
Exploder
A bloated zombie that explodes when close to players, causing area damage.
Screamer
A special undead creature capable of attracting additional zombies by emitting a terrifying scream.
Stalker
A fast, stealth-oriented zombie that hides in dark areas and ambushes players.
The Abomination
A massive boss zombie with mutated limbs, enormous strength, and multiple attack phases.
6. WEAPON SYSTEM
Include a large collection of realistic firearms.
Assault rifles
M4A1
AK-47
SCAR-H
HK416
FAMAS
Submachine guns
MP5
Vector
UMP45
P90
Shotguns
Remington 870
Benelli M4
AA-12
Sniper rifles
Barrett M82
M40A5
Intervention
Light machine guns
M249
RPK
PKM
Pistols
Glock 17
Desert Eagle
1911
Revolver
Special weapons
Experimental energy rifle.
Heavy explosive launcher.
Military flamethrower.
Prototype plasma weapon.
Each firearm must have:
Unique damage.
Unique fire rate.
Unique recoil.
Unique reload speed.
Unique ammunition capacity.
Unique sound effects.
Unique animations.
Upgrade potential.
7. WEAPON UPGRADE SYSTEM
Create an upgrade machine called the WAR FORGE.
Players can spend accumulated points to upgrade weapons.
Weapon upgrades include:
Increased damage.
Increased ammunition capacity.
Faster reload.
Improved accuracy.
Increased fire rate.
Special ammunition.
Enhanced weapon appearance.
At higher upgrade levels, weapons should receive unique visual effects and improved performance.
8. POINTS AND ECONOMY
Players earn points by:
Killing zombies.
Getting headshots.
Repairing barricades.
Completing objectives.
Reviving teammates.
Eliminating special enemies.
Defeating bosses.
Points can be spent on:
New weapons.
Ammunition.
Weapon upgrades.
Perks.
Restricted doors.
Traps.
Equipment.
Display the player's current points clearly on the HUD.
9. PERK SYSTEM
Create interactive perk machines throughout the maps.
Available perks:
QUICK HANDS: Faster weapon reloads.
IRON SKIN: Increased player health.
DEAD EYE: Improved weapon accuracy and reduced recoil.
RAPID FIRE: Increased weapon firing speed.
SPRINTER: Increased movement speed and stamina.
SECOND WIND: Faster teammate revives.
SCAVENGER: Increased ammunition drops.
LAST STAND: Temporary survival boost when critically injured.
Players should have limited perk slots, requiring strategic decisions.
10. MAP DESIGN
Create multiple large, detailed, explorable zombie survival maps.
MAP 1: BLACKWATER MILITARY BASE
A classified military research installation that has been overrun by zombies.
Locations:
Military barracks.
Weapon storage.
Underground laboratories.
Watchtowers.
Vehicle garages.
Medical facilities.
Underground research bunker.
Atmosphere:
Dark nighttime environment, heavy rain, military searchlights, electrical failures, abandoned vehicles, and distant explosions.
MAP 2: DEAD CITY
An abandoned modern city overrun by the undead.
Locations:
Downtown streets.
Apartment buildings.
Police station.
Shopping mall.
Underground subway.
Rooftop access.
Hospital.
Atmosphere:
Burning vehicles, destroyed streets, broken streetlights, abandoned cars, fog, and distant zombie screams.
MAP 3: OPERATION FROSTBITE
A remote military research station in the frozen wilderness.
Locations:
Snow-covered military base.
Research laboratories.
Underground tunnels.
Radio tower.
Armory.
Frozen storage facility.
Atmosphere:
Blizzards, limited visibility, frozen bodies, abandoned military equipment, and freezing temperatures.
MAP 4: THE UNDERGROUND
A massive underground bunker system containing classified experiments.
Locations:
Experimental laboratories.
Prison cells.
Reactor chamber.
Maintenance tunnels.
Underground command center.
Biological containment area.
Atmosphere:
Emergency lighting, red warning lights, leaking pipes, toxic gas, and experimental creatures.
11. BOSS ENCOUNTERS
Create unique boss fights with cinematic introductions.
THE ABOMINATION
A gigantic mutated creature with multiple limbs and devastating melee attacks.
THE WARDEN
A heavily armored undead military commander carrying a massive weapon.
THE DEVOURER
A grotesque creature capable of summoning smaller zombies.
PROJECT ZERO
A failed military experiment that evolves throughout the encounter.
Bosses must have:
Large detailed character models.
Unique attack animations.
Multiple combat phases.
Unique health bars.
Special abilities.
Cinematic entrance sequences.
Unique rewards.
12. HUD AND USER INTERFACE
Create a clean, modern military-style HUD.
Display:
Current round.
Zombie kill count.
Player points.
Current weapon.
Ammunition count.
Grenade count.
Health status.
Armor status.
Perks.
Teammate status.
Include an optional minimap.
Use a dark military interface with subtle red warning elements.
13. MULTIPLAYER CO-OP
Support:
Solo survival.
Two-player cooperative survival.
Four-player online cooperative survival.
Include:
Shared round progression.
Individual point balances.
Teammate reviving.
Downed player mechanics.
Team scoreboards.
Shared boss encounters.
Player-specific weapon loadouts.
Players should be able to communicate through voice chat and optional text chat.
14. SOUND DESIGN
Use immersive, cinematic audio.
Weapon sounds must have:
Distinct firing sounds.
Mechanical reload sounds.
Shell casing impacts.
Bullet impacts.
Environmental echoes.
Zombie sounds must include:
Growling.
Screaming.
Footsteps.
Wall impacts.
Breathing.
Attack sounds.
Environmental audio:
Distant explosions.
Military radio transmissions.
Electrical buzzing.
Rain.
Wind.
Alarms.
Breaking glass.
Distant gunfire.
Use spatial 3D audio so players can determine the direction of approaching enemies.
15. MUSIC
Create an atmospheric original soundtrack.
Use:
Dark cinematic orchestral music.
Heavy percussion.
Industrial sound effects.
Tension-building ambient drones.
Intense combat music.
Music intensity should dynamically increase as zombie hordes become larger and more dangerous.
16. PROGRESSION AND REWARDS
Players earn experience for:
Zombie kills.
Headshots.
Completing rounds.
Boss eliminations.
Easter eggs.
Survival milestones.
Unlock:
New playable characters.
Weapon skins.
Character outfits.
Weapon attachments.
Starting loadouts.
Calling cards.
Player emblems.
Add a persistent player profile and statistics system.
Track:
Highest round survived.
Total zombie kills.
Total headshots.
Bosses defeated.
Total playtime.
Favorite weapons.
Total victories.
17. EASTER EGGS AND SECRETS
Every map should contain hidden secrets.
Include:
Hidden weapon blueprints.
Secret rooms.
Cryptic radio transmissions.
Classified documents.
Hidden boss encounters.
Multi-stage environmental puzzles.
Secret weapon unlocks.
Some Easter eggs should require multiple players to complete.
18. FINAL GRAPHICAL REQUIREMENTS
The game must prioritize AAA-quality visuals.
Target:
Photorealistic character models.
High-poly weapon models.
4K-quality textures where hardware permits.
Physically based materials.
Advanced global illumination.
High-quality reflections.
Realistic shadows.
Volumetric lighting.
Advanced particle effects.
Realistic environmental destruction.
Cinematic animation quality.
Use level-of-detail systems, occlusion culling, optimized lighting, and scalable graphics settings to maintain playable performance.
Create separate Low, Medium, High, and Ultra graphical presets.
19. FINAL DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTION
Generate a fully playable first-person zombie survival game called CALL OF ZOMBIES: ROUND WAR.
Do not create merely a cinematic demonstration or static environment.
The finished game must include:
Functional first-person movement.
Fully functional weapons.
Working reload and shooting mechanics.
Intelligent zombie AI.
Increasing zombie rounds.
Points and purchasing.
Weapon upgrades.
Perk machines.
Interactive doors.
Multiple maps.
Boss encounters.
Multiplayer-ready architecture.
Complete HUD.
Game-over and restart systems.
Prioritize a polished, fully playable core experience before expanding into additional maps and features.
The first playable version must include one complete map, at least five zombie types, ten functional firearms, working round progression, a points economy, weapon purchasing, and one boss encounter.
The final result should feel like a premium, modern military zombie survival game with terrifying atmosphere, realistic graphics, satisfying gunplay, and endless replayability.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"
